correctness.rationale: The exact group multiplication law gives all cycles of both forbiddance permutations, so Lucas independent-set counts yield the formula for every n≥2. All finite signs 2≤n≤40 were evaluated with arbitrary-precision integer arithmetic in verify.py; n≤15 were independently checked by direct permutation cycles, and n=2,3,4 by exhaustive subset enumeration. The bound B(n)≤M(n) follows from L_m≤7^(m/4) for m≥3 and 3√7<8. The exact inequality 3B(41)=105308709116820901835784452756627203197>0 and monotonicity of B(n)/9^n complete the infinite proof. Limit: sign of first raw moment only.

originality.rationale: The all-subset dicyclic first-moment sign at the exact threshold n=30 requires evaluating all cardinalities and proving the sign for an infinite group family. Theorem 7.6 of the focal paper is a general computable representation but does not specialize to the 30-threshold. Fixed-cardinality statements of Mandal and Neetu do not imply the summed sign. Indexed subgroup-graph or commutativity findings concern different invariants. Direct examination of the two highly relevant full preprints, focused web searches, and six semantic research-result queries identified no covering sign theorem. This is evidence of noncoverage in the identified literature, not a proof of worldwide uniqueness.
residual_risks: Mathematical-index retrieval cannot rule out an unindexed unpublished computation or a result with an obscure equivalent formulation.
The finite sign scan is an executable exact-integer certificate, not an independent formal theorem prover; its separate analytical derivation and spot checks are supplied.
General sign of the first moment does not prove product-/quotient-dominance of subset counts.

value.rationale: The focal number-theory article isolates dicyclic first moments as an unmet natural group-family calculation crucial to its moment method. The theorem gives one exact integer threshold for all orders, with an explicit Lucas formula, a nontrivial 9^n-versus-smaller-terms mechanism, and complete finite cutoff proof. It is a motivated full structural sign classification rather than a selected arbitrary finite slice. It does not claim the stronger dominance result.
